history.dynasty: Gajapati dynasty (legend: Gajapati King Purushottama Deva, 15th century)
history.period: Legend: 15th century (actual temple construction date undocumented)
history.summary: The Siddha Vinayaka (Panchama Ganesh) Temple at Panchama village, Golanthara block, Ganjam district, is the most famous Ganapati shrine of the Berhampur region. Legend says that the Gajapati King Purushottama Deva of Puri (15th century), on his way to the conquest of the Kanchi kingdom, recovered the image in the hollow of two trees of Bara and Ashwattha (two large ficus trees) and paid homage after its consecration; the idol still remains inside the trunk of the two trees, with a temple constructed around it. The shrine is an important centre of Ganapataya worship preserving the Panchadevata tradition of Odisha, drawing around 200,000 devotees from Odisha and Andhra Pradesh on Ganesh Chaturthi. CSV town correction: the CSV lists 'Berhampur', which is the nearest city (the temple is ~12 km away at Panchama, near Randha/Golanthara). Identity flag: a separate modern Siddhi Vinayak Mandira on Hill Patna Main Rd inside Brahmapur city (one of the city's most-reviewed temples) shares the name; this file documents the famous historic Panchama shrine as the best-supported referent for a temples dataset. No verified image could be found after genuine searching (the only confirmed Panchama temple images were on a host unreachable from here) - media left empty. Opening hours below are from a single Justdial listing - verify locally.

name: Siddha Vinayaka Temple

town_description: Panchama is a village in Golanthara block, Ganjam district, Odisha, about 12 km from Berhampur (Brahmapur) on the Chennai-Howrah corridor. It is famous almost entirely for the Siddha Vinayaka shrine and the huge Ganesh Chaturthi gathering it draws from Odisha and neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.
tradition: Ganapatya (Ganapati worship; associated with the Panchadevata tradition of Odisha)

travel.road: Panchama is near Randha/Golanthara, about 12 km from Berhampur city; reachable by road via NH16 and local roads (verify route locally).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather; Ganesh Chaturthi (August-September) is the grandest festival but extremely crowded.
